facts.title: Experience League: Edge Delivery Services Overview
facts.quote: Edge Delivery Services is a modern content delivery framework that re-imagines how websites are built and delivered, optimizing for speed, simplicity, and scalability. It is a core part of Adobe Experience Manager and enables faster digital experiences by pushing rendering and delivery closer to the user, at the edge of the network.
facts.supports: Adobe defines Edge Delivery Services as a content delivery framework, part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability.

facts.title: Experience League: Edge Delivery Services Overview
facts.quote: It is not a replacement for a content delivery network (CDN), but it integrates seamlessly with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.
facts.supports: Edge Delivery Services works with the client's own CDN or the Adobe-managed CDN that is included.

facts.title: Experience League: Edge Delivery Services Overview
facts.quote: Edge Delivery Services uses GitHub so you can manage and deploy code directly from your GitHub repository. New content is added instantly without a rebuild process.
facts.supports: Code is managed and deployed from a GitHub repository, and new content needs no rebuild.

facts.title: aem.live: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: Every AEM project should produce a lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop from Google Pagespeed insights on its respective .aem.live site.
facts.supports: Adobe's go-live checklist sets a Lighthouse score of 100 on mobile and desktop as what a project should produce.

facts.title: aem.live: Web Performance, Keeping your Lighthouse Score 100
facts.quote: It turns out that it is hard to improve your Lighthouse score once it is low, but it is not hard to keep it at 100 if you continuously test.
facts.supports: Adobe's advice is to test continuously to keep the Lighthouse score at 100.

facts.title: aem.live: Architecture
facts.quote: The bottom tier is where content can be ingested from: AEM Authoring, which includes Document Authoring (DA) as well as AEM Sites Author, Microsoft SharePoint (Word and Excel), or Google Drive (Docs and Sheets).
facts.supports: The content sources Edge Delivery Services takes content from: AEM Authoring (Document Authoring and AEM Sites Author), Microsoft SharePoint and Google Drive.

facts.title: aem.live: Architecture
facts.quote: Authors get an instant URL to preview their content changes and share with others for review.
facts.supports: Authors preview a change at its own URL and share it for review before publishing.

facts.title: aem.live: Importing Content
facts.quote: The importer offers the tooling to automate the process for multiple pages of a site to be imported and converted.
facts.supports: Adobe's importer automates importing and converting many pages of an existing site.

facts.title: aem.live: Importing Content
facts.quote: It is good practice to make example imports of each page type you wish to import. You can thereby confirm that the authors find the resulting structures intuitive.
facts.supports: Adobe recommends example imports of each page type so authors can confirm the content structure.

facts.title: aem.live: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: In most migrations there are legacy URLs that are retired. Make sure those are reflected in your redirects spreadsheet
facts.supports: Retired URLs go into the redirects spreadsheet before go-live.

facts.title: Experience League: AEM Sites Optimizer
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Sites Optimizer is a cloud-based service that analyzes and improves the performance of websites built on AEM. Sites Optimizer identifies areas for improvement in page loading, component usage, and content delivery.
facts.supports: Adobe defines Sites Optimizer as a cloud-based service that analyzes and improves the performance of websites built on AEM.

facts.title: Experience League: Sites Optimizer Opportunities Documentation
facts.quote: Each opportunity offers insights into the potential business value, highlights areas that need attention, and provides actionable recommendations for optimization.
facts.supports: What an opportunity in Sites Optimizer gives: the potential business value, the areas that need attention and recommendations.

facts.title: Experience League: Broken Backlinks Opportunity Documentation
facts.quote: The broken backlinks opportunity identifies external links pointing to non-existent (404) pages on your site.
facts.supports: Sites Optimizer finds external links that point to missing pages on the site.

facts.title: Experience League: Invalid or missing metadata Opportunity Documentation
facts.quote: The invalid or missing metadata opportunity identifies missing or faulty metadata on your web pages.
facts.supports: Sites Optimizer finds missing or faulty metadata on pages.

facts.title: Experience League: Sites Optimizer Settings
facts.quote: The Google Search Console settings connector in AEM Sites Optimizer enables the analysis of key SEO metrics like search rankings, click-through rates, and Core Web Vitals.
facts.supports: The Google Search Console connector brings search rankings, click-through rates and Core Web Vitals into the analysis.

facts.title: Experience League: Core Web Vitals Opportunity Documentation
facts.quote: AEM Sites Optimizer continuously monitors site performance by using Operational Telemetry to detect regressions in Core Web Vitals metrics such as Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) and Interaction to Next Paint (INP).
facts.supports: Sites Optimizer monitors site performance continuously and detects Core Web Vitals regressions from Operational Telemetry.

facts.title: Experience League: Core Web Vitals Opportunity Documentation
facts.quote: All updates follow standard development practices, requiring review and approval before being merged into production.
facts.supports: Code fixes from Sites Optimizer are reviewed and approved before they are merged into production.

facts.title: Experience League: Deploying to Author Documentation
facts.quote: AEM Sites Optimizer applies the selected optimizations into the authoring environment only
facts.supports: Selected optimizations go into the authoring environment only, not to the live site.

facts.title: Experience League: Deploying to Author Documentation
facts.quote: The AEM author can then review and publish the changes from the Content Management System (CMS), consistent with each opportunity's own Auto-optimize workflow.
facts.supports: An AEM author reviews and publishes the changes from the CMS.

facts.title: Experience League: Sites Optimizer Basics
facts.quote: The Site Summary section provides a snapshot of your site's performance, how Sites Optimizer has improved your site over time, and opportunities for improvement.
facts.supports: The dashboard's site summary reports the site's performance, the improvement over time and the open opportunities.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Assets as a Cloud Service is a cloud-native, Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) solution for Digital Asset Management (DAM) and Dynamic Media
facts.supports: Adobe defines AEM Assets as a Cloud Service as its cloud-native solution for digital asset management and Dynamic Media.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: Adobe provides robust Digital Asset Management (DAM) solutions that help you maximize the value of your digital assets across creation, management, and delivery.
facts.supports: The purpose Adobe gives: to maximize the value of digital assets across creation, management and delivery.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: Ingestion is the process of bringing digital assets into the AEM Assets as a Cloud Service repository so they can be managed, enriched, and delivered.
facts.supports: Assets are brought into the AEM Assets repository to be managed, enriched and delivered.

facts.title: Experience League: Bulk import assets using Assets view
facts.quote: Bulk Import in Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Assets view enables administrators to import large numbers of assets directly from an external data source into AEM Assets in a single, streamlined operation.
facts.supports: Bulk Import brings large numbers of assets in from an external data source in one operation.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) automatically applies smart tags to uploaded assets, by default.
facts.supports: Smart tags are applied to uploaded assets automatically, by default.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: These features include AI-generated tagging (smart tags), customized metadata, and enhanced search capabilities.
facts.supports: How AEM Assets helps people find the right asset: smart tags, customized metadata and enhanced search.

facts.title: Experience League: Introducing Assets as a Cloud Service for Digital Asset Management in AEM
facts.quote: metadata forms let you add custom, business-specific metadata fields directly to an asset's Details page
facts.supports: Metadata forms add the client's own metadata fields to an asset's details page.

facts.title: Experience League: Deploy Content Hub
facts.quote: Content Hub is an add-on for Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service that centralizes and distributes approved brand and marketing content.
facts.supports: Content Hub is an add-on to AEM Assets that centralizes and distributes approved brand and marketing content.

facts.title: Experience League: Deploy Content Hub
facts.quote: Only assets marked Approved on Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service become available for distribution on Content Hub
facts.supports: Only assets marked Approved in AEM Assets reach Content Hub.

facts.title: Experience League: Reports about usage and sharing
facts.quote: The reports provide useful information about your system's usage, how users interact with assets, and which assets are shared.
facts.supports: Asset reports cover system usage, how users interact with assets and which assets are shared.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Manager Forms as a Cloud Service offers a cloud-native, Platform as a Service (PaaS) solution for businesses to create, manage, publish, and update complex digital forms while integrating submitted data with back-end processes, business rules, and saving data in an external data store.
facts.supports: Adobe defines AEM Forms as a Cloud Service: create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms, integrating submitted data with back-end processes and business rules and saving it in an external data store.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: The organization can use AEM Forms as a Cloud Service to create digital forms, connect forms to existing data sources, integrate forms with Adobe Sign to add e-signatures to forms, and generate Document of Record (DoR) to archive submitted forms as PDF files.
facts.supports: Forms connect to existing data sources, integrate with Adobe Sign for e-signatures and can be archived as PDF files once submitted.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: Use forms-centric workflows to automate the processing and routing of form data to various stakeholders, such as managers or departments, for review, approval, or further processing.
facts.supports: Forms-centric workflows route form data to managers or departments for review, approval or further processing.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: It does so by ensuring consistent and auditable processing of form data, automate manual tasks, provide role-based access control, and help comply with regulatory requirements.
facts.supports: Those workflows give consistent and auditable processing of form data and role-based access control.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: The service integrates with Adobe Analytics that lets you capture and track performance metrics for your published forms. The objective behind analyzing these metrics is to make informed decisions based on data about the changes required to make forms or document more usable. You can use Adobe Analytics to discover interaction patterns and problems users face while using adaptive forms.
facts.supports: AEM Forms integrates with Adobe Analytics to track performance metrics for published forms and to show interaction patterns and the problems users face.

facts.title: Experience League: Form builder: Create forms with core components
facts.quote: If you are creating new forms, Adobe recommends using Adaptive Forms Core Components to create an Adaptive Forms.
facts.supports: Adobe recommends Adaptive Forms Core Components for new forms.

facts.title: Experience League: How to integrate Adobe Acrobat Sign with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: Adobe Acrobat Sign enables e-signature workflows for Adaptive Forms and AEM Workflows.
facts.supports: Adobe Acrobat Sign adds e-signature workflows to adaptive forms and AEM workflows.

facts.title: Experience League: How to use the rule editor to add rules to form fields to add dynamic behavior and build complex logic to an adaptive form based on core components?
facts.quote: These rules define actions to trigger on form objects based on preset conditions, user inputs, and user actions on the form.
facts.supports: The rule editor's rules trigger actions on form objects from conditions, user inputs and user actions.

facts.title: Experience League: How to connect a database to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service?
facts.quote: When you connect Adaptive Form to a Database, it requires integration with data sources to fetch customer data while rendering forms. There are use cases when data is fetched from data sources based on user inputs in Adaptive Forms. In addition, when you send an Adaptive Form to a database, the submitted Adaptive Form data can be written back to update the respective data sources.
facts.supports: A form connected to data sources fetches customer data while it renders, and submitted data can be written back to those sources.

facts.title: Experience League: How to configure a Submit Action for an Adaptive Form?
facts.quote: You can configure various submit actions to send form data to services like OneDrive, SharePoint, Workfront Fusion, and more.
facts.supports: Submit actions send form data to services such as OneDrive, SharePoint and Workfront Fusion.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Admin User Guides
facts.quote: Adobe Commerce is an agile B2B and B2C commerce platform which enables merchants and brands to accelerate revenue through customer-centric digital commerce experiences across online and physical spaces.
facts.supports: Adobe defines Adobe Commerce as a B2B and B2C commerce platform for digital commerce experiences across online and physical spaces.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Admin User Guides
facts.quote: The Admin features powerful marketing, search engine optimization, and product management tools that give you the power to create sites that are tailored to your unique business needs.
facts.supports: The Commerce Admin has marketing, search engine optimization and product management tools.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Commerce Admin Getting Started Guide
facts.quote: Learn about the Commerce Admin, the place where merchants set up products and promotions, manage orders, and perform other administrative tasks.
facts.supports: Products, promotions and orders are managed in the Commerce Admin.

facts.title: Experience League: Implementation Playbook
facts.quote: From the early stages of project scoping through development, integrations, and deployment to ongoing support, there are many methodologies and best practices that you need to consider to successfully launch an Adobe Commerce project.
facts.supports: Adobe's implementation playbook covers a Commerce project from scoping through development, integrations and deployment to ongoing support.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to Adobe Commerce B2B
facts.quote: It accommodates companies with complex organizational structures and multiple users with various roles and levels of purchasing permission.
facts.supports: Adobe Commerce B2B supports buying companies with complex structures and users with different roles and purchasing permissions.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to Adobe Commerce B2B
facts.quote: Shared catalogs are the pricing levels that allow setting custom prices per product for different companies on one or multiple websites.
facts.supports: Shared catalogs set custom prices per product for different companies.

facts.title: Experience League: What is Live Search?
facts.quote: Live Search is a feature that replaces the standard search capabilities in Adobe Commerce.
facts.supports: Live Search replaces the standard search in Adobe Commerce.

facts.title: Experience League: What Are Product Recommendations?
facts.quote: Product Recommendations use Adobe AI and machine learning trained on aggregated shopper behavior and catalog data to deliver personalized recommendations on Adobe Commerce storefronts.
facts.supports: Product Recommendations use Adobe AI trained on aggregated shopper behavior and catalog data to personalize recommendations on the storefront.

facts.title: Experience League: Data Connection Introduction
facts.quote: The Data Connection extension connects your Adobe Commerce web instance to the Adobe Experience Platform and the Edge Network.
facts.supports: The Data Connection extension connects Adobe Commerce to Adobe Experience Platform and the Edge Network.

facts.title: Experience League: Data Connection Introduction
facts.quote: Data Connection collects behavioral (storefront) data from the browser, back office data from Commerce servers, and profile data.
facts.supports: The data the extension collects: behavioral storefront data, back office data and profile data.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Marketo Engage Documentation
facts.quote: Adobe Marketo Engage is the world's largest marketing automation platform and a singular solution that lets you attract, segment, and nurture customers.
facts.supports: Adobe describes Marketo Engage as a marketing automation platform that lets you attract, segment and nurture customers.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Programs
facts.quote: Programs represent a single marketing initiative.
facts.supports: Each marketing initiative in Marketo Engage is a program.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Smart Campaigns
facts.quote: The Smart List is how you define who you want to target with your Smart Campaign. It has filters and triggers.
facts.supports: A Smart Campaign's Smart List defines who is targeted, with filters and triggers.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Smart Campaigns
facts.quote: The flow includes the steps you want the Smart Campaign to perform, including Wait steps and split choices.
facts.supports: A Smart Campaign's flow holds the steps it performs, including wait steps and split choices.

facts.title: Experience League: Plan for a New Marketo Engage Implementation
facts.quote: Configuring admin settings including CNAMEs and Munchkin Code.
facts.supports: Adobe's implementation plan includes configuring admin settings, CNAMEs and the Munchkin code.

facts.title: Experience League: Plan for a New Marketo Engage Implementation
facts.quote: Testing automation workflows and data sync
facts.supports: Adobe's implementation plan includes testing the automation workflows and the data sync.

facts.title: Experience League: Add Munchkin Tracking Code to Your Website
facts.quote: Marketo's custom JavaScript tracking code, called Munchkin, tracks all individuals who visit your website so you can react to their visits with automated marketing campaigns.
facts.supports: Munchkin, Marketo's JavaScript tracking code, tracks website visitors so automated campaigns can react to their visits.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding the Salesforce Sync
facts.quote: The sync between Salesforce and Marketo is bidirectional only for leads, contacts, and Salesforce campaigns. In these cases, whenever you make changes in either Salesforce or Marketo, your updates will be reflected in both systems. All other syncs are from Salesforce to Marketo only.
facts.supports: The Salesforce sync is bidirectional for leads, contacts and Salesforce campaigns only; everything else syncs from Salesforce to Marketo.

facts.title: Experience League: Report Type Overview
facts.quote: Review interactions with your emails: delivered or bounced, opened, clicked, unsubscribed, etc.
facts.supports: The Email Performance report covers delivered, bounced, opened, clicked and unsubscribed.

facts.title: Experience League: Report Type Overview
facts.quote: View visits, conversions, and other metrics for your landing pages.
facts.supports: The Landing Page Performance report covers visits, conversions and other metrics.

facts.title: Experience League: Acrobat Tutorials
facts.quote: Adobe Acrobat, an Adobe Document Cloud solution, helps keep business moving by converting, editing, sharing, and signing PDFs.
facts.supports: What Adobe Acrobat does: converts, edits, shares and signs PDFs.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: These APIs automate the generation, manipulation, and transformation of document content via a set of modern cloud-based web services.
facts.supports: The Acrobat Services APIs automate generating, manipulating and transforming document content through cloud-based web services.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: You can easily create a PDF from a dynamic HTML report, set a password to prevent unauthorized opening of the document, compress it for sharing as an attachment, or extract text, tables, images and document structure to enable downstream solutions.
facts.supports: Examples of what the PDF Services API automates: creating a PDF from HTML, password protection, compression and extracting content.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: Using Document Generation API, you can merge your data(e.g. JSON file) with Word templates to create dynamic documents for contracts and agreements, invoices, proposals, reports, forms, branded marketing documents and more.
facts.supports: The Document Generation API merges data with Word templates to create contracts, invoices, proposals, reports and other documents.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: The PDF Embed API brings PDF viewing to any web application with only a few lines of JavaScript.
facts.supports: The PDF Embed API puts a PDF viewer into a web application with a few lines of JavaScript.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: Document collaboration is achieved with support for commenting, drawing, highlighting, and text editing tools.
facts.supports: The embedded viewer supports commenting, drawing, highlighting and text editing tools.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: The PDF Accessibility Auto-Tag API is a powerful tool that may be used as part of the process of improving accessibility in individual PDFs and can be applied at scale for large backlogs of PDFs. Auto-tagging adds document structure tags to the PDF file that are used to read a document's text and present it in a way that makes sense to users using assistive technology.
facts.supports: The Auto-Tag API adds the structure tags assistive technology uses to read a PDF, one file at a time or at scale for backlogs.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: The output from the API is a tagged PDF, but it is not guaranteed to fully comply with accessibility standards such as WCAG and PDF/UA, as you may need to perform further downstream remediation and it is your responsibility to seek independent review of the same to meet those standards.
facts.supports: Auto-tagged output is not guaranteed to comply fully with WCAG and PDF/UA; further remediation and independent review may be needed.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: PDF Electronic Seal API
facts.quote: PDF Electronic Seal API is a cloud based solution to apply an electronic seal on PDF documents using the digital certificates issued to organizations to demonstrate the integrity and authenticity of official documents such as invoices, statements etc.
facts.supports: The PDF Electronic Seal API seals PDF documents with an organization's digital certificate to show their integrity and authenticity.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction
facts.quote: The default region uses the United States to process documents. Developers can now also use the European region (Ireland) for API calls.
facts.supports: PDF Services processes documents in the United States by default; the European region (Ireland) can be chosen for API calls.

facts.title: Experience League: Integrate AEM with Acrobat Sign
facts.quote: Adobe Acrobat Sign is a digital signature service offered by Adobe that allows users to electronically sign and collect signatures on documents.
facts.supports: Adobe defines Acrobat Sign as its digital signature service for signing documents electronically and collecting signatures.

facts.title: Experience League: Acrobat Sign Tutorials
facts.quote: Acrobat Sign, an Adobe Document Cloud solution, scales to meet your organization's needs with integrations, APIs, advanced authentication, additional admin features, and more.
facts.supports: Acrobat Sign scales with integrations, APIs, advanced authentication and admin features.

facts.title: Experience League: Create a Reusable Template
facts.quote: Learn how to create a reusable document template and add it to your Acrobat Sign library for future use. Document templates provide speed and consistency in your sign transactions and the ability to manage document revisions and changes.
facts.supports: Reusable document templates in the Acrobat Sign library give speed and consistency and a way to manage document revisions.

facts.title: Experience League: Build a Custom Workflow
facts.quote: Learn how to create and use custom workflows to speed up the process of creating and sending an agreement.
facts.supports: Custom workflows speed up creating and sending an agreement.

facts.title: Experience League: Creating a Web Form
facts.quote: Learn how to create a document that can be signed electronically directly on your website. You can create a hosted hyperlink to your form or use the link to embed on your website in html or JavaScript.
facts.supports: A web form is a document people sign electronically on the client's website, through a hosted link or embedded in a page.

facts.title: Experience League: Send in Bulk
facts.quote: Everyone gets their own document to sign, and you can track the progress of each individual that you've sent the document to
facts.supports: With Send in Bulk each recipient gets their own document to sign and progress is tracked per person.

facts.title: Experience League: Audit Reports
facts.quote: Every document in Acrobat Sign passes through a series of event "milestones" that define the progress of a transaction. These milestones are thoroughly documented in an audit report for every transaction.
facts.supports: Every transaction has an audit report that documents the milestones the document passed through.

facts.title: Experience League: Reporting and Transaction Usage
facts.quote: These reports can include information such as the percentage of agreements that have been signed or the average time it takes to sign.
facts.supports: Reports can show the percentage of agreements signed and the average time to sign.

facts.title: Experience League: Integrations Overview
facts.quote: You can use Acrobat Sign inside other applications your organization already uses, such as Microsoft, Salesforce, Workday, and Marketo to name a few.
facts.supports: Acrobat Sign works inside applications such as Microsoft, Salesforce and Workday.

facts.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Sign API
facts.quote: Acrobat Sign service features are available via easy-to-use REST APIs.
facts.supports: Acrobat Sign's features are available through REST APIs.

the submitted Adaptive Form data can be written back to update the respective data sources

generate Document of Record (DoR) to archive submitted forms as PDF files

create and use custom workflows to speed up the process of creating and sending an agreement
